verdict.rationale: Phaser's architecture is inherently event-driven — a unified input system (phaser-docs-9), physics with collision/velocity/gravity handling (phaser-docs-8, phaser-docs-46), frame-based animation sequencing (phaser-docs-11, phaser-docs-25, phaser-docs-48), and scene lifecycle events like pause/resume/sleep (phaser-docs-23) all imply developers can bind actions to in-game events. However, the evidence never shows an explicit 'define a rule that triggers an action' API (e.g. .on('collide', callback) or event-listener syntax) or any AI-native rule-authoring interface. Missing for 10: explicit event-listener/rule-binding documentation, code examples showing rule-to-action wiring, and any AI-specific automation-rule tooling beyond the MCP code-generation agent.
